subject: Banking
title: Dark Pools
description: A quick, practical guide to Dark Pools.

hook.text: Dark pools are private exchanges where large investors trade millions of shares without anyone seeing the order until.

buildup.text: If a pension fund puts a 5-million-share sell order on a public exchange, the price would crash before the order fills.

discovery.text: Dark pools match large orders anonymously. The trade happens at market price without alerting other traders.

twist.text: Dark pools now handle about 40% of all US stock trading. The majority of volume happens where you cannot see it.

climax.text: Dark pools protect large traders but reduce market transparency.

punchline.text: 40% of US stock trading is invisible. Dark pools hide real volume.

quiz.question: Why do institutional investors use dark pools?
options: To execute large trades without moving the market price against them
